overall: Atlanta is sitting at a flat 77.0°F as of 07:19 ET with zero warming velocity and a high dewpoint of 71.6°F, indicating a very warm, muggy airmass that has kept overnight lows unusually elevated. The sky is heavily overcast (BKN, 100% cloud fraction) with a very low ceiling (~396m), which is suppressing early morning solar heating but may burn off by mid-morning ahead of the expected afternoon peak around 13.9h ET. Temperature has been essentially locked at 77°F since midnight with no measurable trend, making the morning start atypically stagnant.
forecast_obs_notes: The three NWP models show moderate disagreement, with HRRR most bullish at 86.2°F, ECMWF at 83.7°F, and NBM most conservative at 81.9°F (averaging ~83.9°F). The META model — the fused daily+intraday model flagged as most reliable — peaks at 86-87°F (28.4%), leaning toward the HRRR end of guidance, while the ensemble odd-bucket signal independently flags 81-82°F as Tier 1 with high confidence (30%), creating meaningful tension between the short-range NWP blend and the ensemble layer.
max_temp_prediction: Balancing the META model's 86-87°F peak probability, NWP guidance averaging ~84°F, and the suppressive effect of heavy low-level clouds and persistent overcast, today's high is most likely to land near 85-86°F — assuming cloud cover erodes sufficiently through midday to allow afternoon heating. Key downside risk is the low ceiling persisting longer than expected, which could cap the high closer to 82-83°F; upside risk would be rapid cloud scour driving temps toward 88°F as the HRRR suggests. Confidence is moderate given the cloud wildcard, with the preponderance of evidence centering around 85.5°F.
